source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀρετὴν εἶναι τὴν φρόνησιν expl. οὐρανοὺς ἡτοίμασεν ὁ κύριος.
thought_title: Prudence as virtue and the preparing of the heavens
orientation: Origen is still commenting on Luke before the argument moves to Matthew's opening.
pass_a_gloss: But since prudence is a virtue expl. the Lord prepared heavens.

choices.why: keeps the cognitive moral sense required by the following clause about preparing heavens
literal moral term in the since clause, not a particular virtue
literal past act of making ready, keeps tense and agency of the Lord
plural object as written, not singular sky

pass_b_english: But since prudence is a virtue … [text omitted in the edition] … "the Lord prepared the heavens" (Proverbs 3:19).
notes: The token expl. is left untranslated as an unexplained abbreviation or editorial marker; the sentence is fragmentary and its connection is uncertain, so only what is present is glossed.
